description: Self-service dashboards and questions over the operator's own databases, so a report is a saved query rather than a spreadsheet mailed around.
licenseNote: AGPL-3.0 covers the open-source edition this entry deploys; JWT/SAML SSO, sandboxing, audit logs and API keys are commercial Pro/Enterprise features and are not included.
authMethod: Proxy gate only: JWT/SAML SSO is a Pro/Enterprise feature, so the open-source edition keeps its own login
packagingSource: vendored definition (platform/upstream/D11-01) pinning the published application image @ v0.65.2 with a pinned PostgreSQL 18 sidecar

integration.authMethod: Session token per user (POST /api/session); API keys are a Pro/Enterprise feature, so the open-source edition brokers a session instead

notes: The sidecar PostgreSQL is required: Metabase's embedded H2 store corrupts under concurrent use and loses saved questions, so the definition runs `postgres:18-alpine` as service `db` and the entry's `database` dependency is served inside it rather than provisioned again. Three secrets have no usable image default and are declared as required: `MB_DB_PASS` (also the sidecar's `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, so it cannot disagree with itself), `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` (without it every connected data-source credential is stored in plaintext) and `MB_SESSION_SECRET_KEY` (without it the session keys in the application database are unsigned and anyone with read access can forge a session). `MB_SITE_URL` is derived from the instance's own route on every deploy, so a second instance gets its own links. `MB_LOAD_SAMPLE_CONTENT=false` keeps first boot from registering the demo `Examples` database and its sample questions; it is read once and removes nothing a previous boot installed. Back up `mb-pgdata`, mounted at `/var/lib/postgresql` (the PostgreSQL 18 image's declared VOLUME), which holds the whole application database. First run redirects to `/setup` until an administrator exists — account creation is a business step, not a deployment step.
deviation: The class is `fa_gate`, and the gap is the edition rather than the definition: JWT/SAML SSO, sandboxing, audit logs and API keys are commercial Pro/Enterprise features, so the open-source image keeps its own login form and the edge's forward-auth gate protects the route without signing anyone in. The integration operations are therefore brokered with a session token minted per user against `/api/session`, and the session maximum of 480 minutes is the platform's policy, not the product's cookie lifetime. Itemised in platform/upstream/D11-01/README.md: the published artefact is the image `metabase/metabase`, because the repository ships a build Dockerfile and no Compose file, and the executor's BuildKit session is refused by the deploy-worker's socket proxy; the container healthcheck asks `/api/health` rather than the socket, because `/` answers `200` with the loading page while the schema is still migrating, and `ready` was measured on a deployment whose product still answered `503 initializing`.
